docs.text: λORM λORM is an ORM that allows us to perform distributed queries on different database engines. In λORM, queries are defined using lambda expressions based on a domain model which abstracts us from the infrastructure. For example, in a query you can obtain or modify records from different entities, where some persist in MySQL, others in Postgres, and others in Mongo. λORM allows you to define different scenarios for the same domain. For example, in one scenario, the infrastructure may consist of distributed instances across SQL Server, MongoDB, and Oracle, while in another scenario it may be a single Postgres instance. This allows the CQRS pattern to be implemented through configuration, without needing to write a single line of code. In addition to being used as a Node.js library, it can be consumed from a command line interface (CLI), or through the Data Gateway : a REST API, MCP for AI agents, a WebSocket API and a web UI, with the clients for Node and other languages. Query Language Example of a query where orders and their details associated with a customer are obtained: const query = (country: string) => Products .map(p => ({ category: p.category.name, largestPrice: max(p.price) })) .filter(p => (p.price > 5 && p.supplier.country == country) || (p.inStock < 3)) .having(p => max(p.price) > 50) .sort(p => desc(p.largestPrice)); // Run the query passing the value of the country parameter const result = await orm.execute(query, { country: 'ARG' }); In this example: Define a query that returns a list of product categories along with the maximum price of each category. Filter products based on price and supplier's country or stock availability Group products by category and calculate the maximum price Map each product to an object with category name and maximum price Sort the products by largest price in descending order view: queries | select | join | grouping | include | insert | bulkInsert | update | delete | repository | usage | metadata Include The include allows us to obtain the entity data and its relationships in the same query. These data may be in different databases. \ In this example the query is expressed as a text string. (Which is another alternative to the lambda expression) import { orm } from '../../lib' (async () => { try { await orm.init('./config/northwind.yaml') const query = `Orders .filter(p => p.id === id) .include(p => [ p.customer.map(p => p.name), p.details .include(p => p.product .include(p => p.category.map(p => p.name)) .map(p => p.name)) .map(p => [p.quantity, p.unitPrice]) ] )` const params = { id: 102 } const result = await orm.execute(query, params, { stage: 'PostgreSQL' }) console.log(JSON.stringify(result, null, 2)) } catch (error:any) { console.error(error.message) } finally { await orm.end() } })() Result: [ { "id": 102, "customerId": "SPLIR", "employeeId": 7, "orderDate": "1996-11-07T23:00:00.000Z", "requiredDate": "1996-12-05T23:00:00.000Z", "shippedDate": "1996-11-14T23:00:00.000Z", "shipViaId": 1, "freight": 8.63, "name": "Split Rail Beer & Ale", "address": "P.O. Box 555", "city": "Lander", "region": "WY", "postalCode": "82520", "country": "USA", "customer": { "name": "Split Rail Beer & Ale" }, "details": [ { "quantity": 24, "unitPrice": 5.9, "product": { "name": "Tourtire", "category": { "name": "Meat/Poultry" } } } ] } ] more info: include Schema Configuration Through the schema, you can define entities, enumerations, indexes, unique keys, default values, constraints, mapping, sources, stages, listeners, etc. The schema can be defined in a JSON or YAML format. Conditions or actions are performed using the same expression language that is used to define queries. view: schema | definition | use | expressions | environment Variables | composite | listener | multiple stages | multiple sources | push | pull | fetch | introspect | incorporate All Labs You can access various labs at lambdaorm labs Related projects λORM CLI : Command line interface for λORM Data Gateway : λORM schemas over REST, MCP and WebSocket, with a web UI Client : Node client for the Data Gateway 3xpr : Extensible expression engine, which allows evaluating mathematical and logical expressions.

docs.text: λORM CLI λORM CLI ( @lambdaorm/cli , 1.6.x) is a command line application to use λORM , locally with a workspace ( -w ) or on a Data Gateway ( -u <url> ). Installation Install the package globally; it adds the lambdaorm command: npm i -g @lambdaorm/cli lambdaorm --version It needs Node 20 or later. The unscoped lambdaorm-cli package is the old, unmaintained one. The Data Gateway's Docker image ( flaviorita/data-gateway ) already includes the CLI. CLI Command Description version Prints the CLI version and the @lambdaorm/lib version the project uses. init Generates the λORM project structure. build Adds configuration, model and repositories according to the language. schema Returns schema information. push Synchronizes the databases with the model ( -o writes the scripts instead). pull Pulls the stage with the sources. fetch Shows the differences between the databases and the model; exit code 1 when there are any. introspect Reads and analyzes data and updates the schema. incorporate Updates the schema, pushes the sources and imports the data. drop Removes all database objects but not the database. import Imports data from a file to the database. export Exports data from a database. execute Executes a query. script Runs a script: several queries in one transaction. plan Returns the execution plan of a query. metadata Returns the metadata of a query. parameters Returns the parameters of a query. model Returns the model of a query. constraints Returns the constraints of a query. lambdaorm <command> -h lists the options of a command. Every command exits with code 1 when it fails (from @lambdaorm/cli 1.6.3). Commands on a Data Gateway ( -u <url> , the URL of the schema: http://gateway:8080/iot/v1 ) send SERVICE_TOKEN from the environment as Authorization: Bearer when it is set (a gateway with bearer authentication ). Usage Commands Infrastructure Commands Version Init Build DDL Commands Push Fetch Drop Pull, Introspect, Incorporate: see Schema synchronization Data Commands Import Export Query Commands Execute Script Plan Metadata Parameters Model Constraints source Change log Labs You can access various labs at github.com/lambda-orm/lambdaorm-labs

docs.text: Changelog All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file. @lambdaorm/cli 1.6.2 Patch Changes e4ce3af: 3xpr 5.2.0 in every package (one copy of it). lib builds each Orm's 3xpr instance with the ExpressionsBuilder 3xpr now exports, instead of importing it from one of its files. b22e580: lambdaorm --version and lambdaorm version print this CLI's version (they printed the version of the project's package.json in the current directory, or looked for the old lambdaorm-cli package). Updated dependencies [e4ce3af] @lambdaorm/base@3.2.1 @lambdaorm/lib@3.2.2 @lambdaorm/client@0.9.1 1.6.1 Patch Changes Updated dependencies [2dc1ac1] Updated dependencies [68faedb] @lambdaorm/lib@3.2.1 1.6.0 Minor Changes 0e683c6: Scripts: several queries in one transaction. client: orm.executeScript(script, data, options) calls the service's POST /script (the service must run with SCRIPT_ENABLED=true ). cli: new lambdaorm script command, with the script inline ( -x ) or in a file ( -f ), its variables in -d ; local with the workspace or on a service with -u . d16b60a: stage.push().sentencesBySource() : the DDL grouped per source (one script per database). cli: lambdaorm push -o <dir> writes one script per source that changes, <stage>.<source>.sql (deterministic names, to rename into a versioned migration); -o without a folder prints the DDL grouped by source — L19. Patch Changes 2ee8930: Upgrade the data7expressions dependencies to their latest major: 3xpr from 1.x to ^5.1.1 , h3lp and typ3s to ^5.0.0 (and json-light to ^5.0.0 in the CLI). No API changes were needed. Behaviour inherited from 3xpr: <= now has the same precedence as the other comparison operators ( a <= b == true used to evaluate as a <= (b == true) ). 3xpr 5.1.0 evaluates async expressions statement by statement (listeners, orm.execute inside expressions), never runs an async function while building an expression, and adds throw , try / catch , return , break and continue ; 3xpr 5.1.1 parses the empty string literal "" (it used to swallow the rest of the expression). ee1e7ac: Packaging: The published exports pointed to ./build/lib/index.js , a path the package doesn't have: require('@lambdaorm/lib') (and base, client) failed for everyone installing from npm. dist now rewrites exports (and bin ) like main — L7. cli: declares bin: lambdaorm , so npm i -g @lambdaorm/cli installs the lambdaorm command — L29. Every package's dist is smoke-tested before it can be released: required by its name (so exports applies) and, for the CLI, lambdaorm --help . 8b8f470: Stage commands: push/DDL: a stage's last source without condition is a catch-all, as in DML: it gets only the entities no other source took (it used to receive every entity) — L25. fetch/pull on PostgreSQL work with reserved words as column names ( order ): the metadata query quoted the column twice — L6, L21. stage.fetch() reports the drift: per mapping, the entities that differ from the model (present in one side only, different columns, types, lengths, required, primary key), each with its differences ; no entities when in step. stage.read() returns the databases' mappings as fetch did (pull uses it) — L22. cli: lambdaorm fetch exits with code 1 when there are differences (for CI). fetch , pull , schema , introspect and incorporate load the --envfile they declared (it was ignored). Version Prints the version of the CLI that runs and the version of @lambdaorm/lib the project uses. Params parameter short describe workspace -w Project path (default: the current directory). language -l Develop language (default node ). Example lambdaorm version Result: lambdaorm cli version: 1.6.2 Local lambdaorm version: 3.2.2 Local lambdaorm not found. when the project doesn't depend on @lambdaorm/lib . To print only the CLI version: lambdaorm --version # or lambdaorm -v 1.6.2

docs.text: Constraints Return constraints associated with the query expression. Params parameter short describe workspace -w project path. query -q Query expression envfile -e Read in a file of environment variables. output -o Generates an output according to the following possible values [json|beautiful|light|yaml] url -u URL of the schema on a Data Gateway Example lambdaorm constraints -o beautiful -q "Orders.filter(p=>p.id==id).include(p=>p.details)" Result: { "entity": "Orders", "constraints": [], "children": [ { "entity": "Orders.details", "constraints": [] } ] }

Params parameter short describe workspace -w project path. stage -s Name of stage query -q Query expression data -d Data (parameters) of the query: JSON, or the path of a JSON file. envfile -e Read in a file of environment variables. output -o Generates an output according to the following possible values [json|beautiful|light|yaml] url -u URL of the schema on a Data Gateway Examples BulkInsert lambdaorm execute -w lab/countries -e lab/countries/.env -q "Countries.bulkInsert().include(p => p.states)" -d ./lab/countries/countries.json Query lambdaorm execute -e ".env" -o beautiful -q "Products.distinct(p => ({ quantity: p.quantity, category: p.category.name })).sort(p => p.category).page(1,3)" Result: [ { "quantity": "10 boxes x 20 bags", "category": "Beverages" }, { "quantity": "24 - 12 oz bottles", "category": "Beverages" }, { "quantity": "12 - 355 ml cans", "category": "Beverages" } ]

docs.text: Fetch Shows the drift between the databases of a stage and the model: per mapping, the entities that differ (missing on one side, different columns, types, lengths, nullability or primary key), each with its differences . The entities are empty when the databases are in step with the model. Relations and indexes are not compared. Exit code 1 when there are differences , so it can be used in CI. Params parameter short describe workspace -w Project path. stage -s Name of stage. envfile -e Read in a file of environment variables. output -o Generates an output according to the following possible values [json|beautiful|light|yaml] url -u URL of the schema on a Data Gateway. Example lambdaorm fetch -w lab/countries -e lab/countries/.env -o beautiful || echo "the database differs from the model" Result: [ { "name": "default", "entities": [ { "name": "Countries", "mapping": "Countries", "differences": ["column phone missing in the database"], "properties": [ ... ] } ] } ] In step: [ { "name": "default", "entities": [] } ]

docs.text: Push Synchronizes the databases of a stage with the model. It compares the model with the databases (what fetch reads), not with the orm_state file: new tables are created with keys, foreign keys and indexes; in existing tables missing columns are added and columns with another type, length or nullability are altered. It never drops what exists only in the database ( fetch reports it). orm_state is still written as a record. Params parameter short describe workspace -w Project path. stage -s Name of stage. envfile -e Read in a file of environment variables. output -o Generates the queries but does not apply them. Alone: prints them per source. With a folder: writes one script per source that changes, <stage>.<source>.sql . force -f If there is an error in a statement, continue executing the next statements. push runs locally only (no -u ). Examples Apply the changes: lambdaorm push -w lab/countries -e lab/countries/.env Write the scripts instead (e.g. to save them as versioned migrations): lambdaorm push -w lab/countries -e lab/countries/.env -s default -o migrations /home/user/lab/countries/migrations/default.default.sql Print them: lambdaorm push -w lab/countries -e lab/countries/.env -o [ { "source": "default", "sentences": [ "ALTER TABLE Countries ADD phone VARCHAR(20)" ] } ] To rename a column, set previousMapping in the property mapping ( { name: icon, mapping: icon_name, previousMapping: icon } ); remove it once applied. Table renames are not supported.

docs.text: Script Runs a script: several queries in one transaction . The script is a 3xpr script whose orm.execute(query, data, options) calls all run in the same transaction, also across sources; it commits when the script ends and rolls back on any error (a query or a throw ). The result is the value of the last statement (or of return ). It runs locally with the workspace ( -w ) or on a Data Gateway ( -u , POST /script ; the gateway must have scripts.enabled and the credential the script permission). Params parameter short describe workspace -w Project path. stage -s Name of stage. script -x Script (3xpr statements calling orm.execute(query, data, options) ). file -f File with the script (instead of -x ). data -d Variables of the script: JSON, or the path of a JSON file. envfile -e Read in a file of environment variables. output -o Generates an output according to the following possible values [json|beautiful|light|yaml] url -u URL of the schema on a Data Gateway ( POST /script ). Examples Inline lambdaorm script -w lab/northwind -e lab/northwind/.env -o beautiful \ -x 'orm.execute("Orders.update(p => ({ freight: freight })).filter(p => p.id == id)", { id: id, freight: freight }); orm.execute("Orders.filter(p => p.id == id)", { id: id })' \ -d '{"id": 10248, "freight": 40}' From a file create-quote.3xpr : account = orm.execute("Accounts.filter(p => p.id == accountId)", { accountId: accountId }); if (account.length() == 0) { throw { status: 404, message: "account not found" }; } orm.execute("Quotes.insert()", { id: quoteId, accountId: accountId, status: "draft" }); for (line in lines) { orm.execute("QuoteLines.insert()", { id: line.id, quoteId: quoteId, quantity: line.qty }); } orm.execute("QuoteEvents.insert()", { quoteId: quoteId, event: "created" }, { stage: "insights" }); quoteId lambdaorm script -w . -f create-quote.3xpr -d quote.json orm.execute(…, { stage: "insights" }) runs on another stage and joins the same transaction (from @lambdaorm/lib 3.3.0). On a Data Gateway lambdaorm script -u http://localhost:8080 -f create-quote.3xpr -d '{"quoteId": 10, "accountId": 1, "lines": []}' Notes Language: variables, if / else , for , for … in , while , switch , try / catch , throw , return ; no ? : operator, no ++ / -- (use i += 1 ), no user-defined functions. The script works on a copy of the data and can't read environment variables ( $VAR fails). Errors are printed as error: … and nothing of the script is written. With -u , a Data Gateway with bearer authentication needs the token in SERVICE_TOKEN in the CLI's environment (sent as Authorization: Bearer ; @lambdaorm/cli 1.6.3). The command exits with code 1 when the script fails (@lambdaorm/cli 1.6.3).

docs.text: Data Gateway Objective Give applications, AI agents and people governed access to the data of λORM schemas over the network , by configuration, without writing a backend for it. A λORM schema already describes a domain (its entities, relations and rules) and where its data lives (one or many databases of different engines). The Data Gateway publishes that schema so that: an application queries and writes it through a REST API (or a WebSocket connection), with the same lambda queries it would use in Node; an AI agent explores the domain and queries it through MCP, knowing the entities and the language; a person explores the schemas, reads each entity as a form, tries queries and draws diagrams in a web UI; and so that who can do what is decided in one place, the same for all of them: each credential has permissions, and every change is audited. Scope What it does: Serves one or several λORM schemas per instance, each at a route ( /iot/v1 , /iot/v2 , /accounts ). Exposes them by four transports , each one only when it has a port: REST ( http ), MCP ( mcpHttp , mcpWebSocket ) and a JSON-RPC API over WebSocket ( webSocket ). Every operation of λORM: queries ( execute , plan , metadata , model , parameters , constraints ), scripts (several queries in one transaction), queued executions (Kafka), the schema and its model, and stages (export, import). Authentication (API key, bearer token, basic) and permissions per credential ( read , write , script , queue , stageImport ), globally, per transport or per schema. Isolation : each schema runs in its own worker, with its own environment and connections; one that fails doesn't affect the others. Audit of writes, metrics (Prometheus), health (Kubernetes probes), limits (rate, concurrency, sizes, time). A web UI : explorer, entity forms, query tabs with autocompletion, saved queries and diagrams of the domain. What it doesn't do: It doesn't define the domain nor migrate the databases: that is the schema and the CLI ( push , pull , …). It doesn't accept SQL: only λORM queries, translated for each source. No users nor roles of its own beyond the credentials of its configuration (no login against an identity provider yet). The UI keeps what is saved in each browser; there is no shared storage of saved queries on the server. Description The Data Gateway is a Node application published as the Docker image flaviorita/data-gateway . It reads one configuration file ( data-gateway.config.yaml ) that says where the schemas are, how they are exposed and who can use them; the schemas themselves stay in their λORM workspaces ( lambdaORM.yaml ). Inside, a supervisor starts and watches the workers. The edge worker listens on the ports of the transports, authenticates each request and sends it, by a direct channel, to the worker of the schema , which checks the permissions, runs the operation with λORM against its databases and audits it. A heavy query in one schema doesn't slow down another; a schema whose database is down answers 503 and is retried, while the others keep working. Concepts Concept What it is Schema a λORM workspace (a folder with lambdaORM.yaml ): domain, sources, mappings, stages; served at a route Route where a schema is reached: /iot/v1/execute , /iot/v1/mcp , ws://host/iot/v1 ; a single schema can be at the root Transport a way in, on its own port: http , mcpHttp , mcpWebSocket , webSocket Credential a key, token or user with a name and permissions ; sent by the client in each request Permission read , write , script , queue , stageImport : what the credential can do, on every transport Stage a λORM scenario of a schema (which sources hold which entities); chosen with options.stage Worker where a schema runs: a thread or a process of its own A request, step by step A client sends POST /iot/v1/execute with X-Api-Key: … and { "query": "Orders.filter(…)", "data": {…} } . The http transport finds the credential ( agent , permissions [read] ) and the schema iot/v1 . The schema's worker analyses the query: it only selects, so read is enough. λORM translates it for each source of the stage, runs it and joins the results. The answer goes back as JSON. Had it written data, the credential would have needed write , and the operation would have left an audit line. In this section Getting started : step by step, from an empty folder to the REST API, the UI, MCP and WebSocket. Configuration : the configuration file, schemas, environment, runtime and every key. Transports : the four transports, their routes and options. REST API : every method of the http transport, with examples. MCP : the tools, resources and transports for AI agents. WebSocket API : the JSON-RPC methods and the notifications. Security : authentication, permissions, audit, limits and errors. UI : the web interface: explorer, entity forms, queries, saved queries and diagrams. Clients : @lambdaorm/client , the CLI and the OpenAPI document. Operations : Docker, Kubernetes, health, metrics and logs. Change log

Isolation : each schema runs in its own worker, with its own environment and connections; one that fails doesn't affect the others. Audit of writes, metrics (Prometheus), health (Kubernetes probes), limits (rate, concurrency, sizes, time). A web UI : explorer, entity forms, query tabs with autocompletion, saved queries and diagrams of the domain. What it doesn't do: It doesn't define the domain nor migrate the databases: that is the schema and the CLI ( push , pull , …). It doesn't accept SQL: only λORM queries, translated for each source. No users nor roles of its own beyond the credentials of its configuration (no login against an identity provider yet). The UI keeps what is saved in each browser; there is no shared storage of saved queries on the server.
docs.title: Scope

docs.text: The Data Gateway is a Node application published as the Docker image flaviorita/data-gateway . It reads one configuration file ( data-gateway.config.yaml ) that says where the schemas are, how they are exposed and who can use them; the schemas themselves stay in their λORM workspaces ( lambdaORM.yaml ). Inside, a supervisor starts and watches the workers. The edge worker listens on the ports of the transports, authenticates each request and sends it, by a direct channel, to the worker of the schema , which checks the permissions, runs the operation with λORM against its databases and audits it. A heavy query in one schema doesn't slow down another; a schema whose database is down answers 503 and is retried, while the others keep working.
docs.title: Description

docs.text: Getting started : step by step, from an empty folder to the REST API, the UI, MCP and WebSocket. Configuration : the configuration file, schemas, environment, runtime and every key. Transports : the four transports, their routes and options. REST API : every method of the http transport, with examples. MCP : the tools, resources and transports for AI agents. WebSocket API : the JSON-RPC methods and the notifications. Security : authentication, permissions, audit, limits and errors. UI : the web interface: explorer, entity forms, queries, saved queries and diagrams. Clients : @lambdaorm/client , the CLI and the OpenAPI document. Operations : Docker, Kubernetes, health, metrics and logs. Change log

docs.text: Change log The versions of the Docker image flaviorita/data-gateway . 3.0.0-rc.4 (2026-11-18) Prerelease: it doesn't move latest . Uses @lambdaorm/lib 3.5.3. Bug Fixes: Swagger ( /doc ): Authorize offers the credential the served schemas are configured with (an API key in its header, a bearer token or basic); it offered a fixed bearer token, so it didn't work with an API key. Each http transport serves its own document. From @lambdaorm/lib 3.5.3: a PostgreSQL bytea column is read as buffer ( lambdaorm pull , fetch and introspect failed with error with type: bytea ), and a buffer property is created as BYTEA . 3.0.0-rc.3 (2026-11-18) Prerelease: it doesn't move latest . Uses @lambdaorm/lib 3.5.2. Features (the UI at /ui , built on @lambdaorm/ui ): Named Data Gateway: a home page with what it is and the schemas, a login page (show / hide the secret) and the query page, with logout; the theme (system / light / dark) and the language (English, Español, Português, Français, Italiano, Deutsch, Nederlands, Català, Galego, Euskara) are chosen at the top and kept in the browser. The credential is never kept. An explorer of the schemas on the left. For each schema: its domain as YAML, read only (only GET /{schema}/domain : never the sources nor the connections); its entities with their properties and relations, and the form of each entity (properties, relations and references, keys, indexes and constraints, rows read only by pages, diagram). Folders, queries and diagrams saved with a name and a description, moved by dragging; queries in tabs with Save, Save as… and Ctrl+S. Saved diagrams: the chosen entities laid out by themselves, boxes and lines moved by hand, boxes taken out with their ×, the names of the relations, export to SVG and PNG. What is saved stays in the browser (IndexedDB, per gateway and user of the credential) and is exported to and imported from a JSON file. Results: a copy icon and an export menu (JSON, YAML, tab-separated text). The Swagger page says Data Gateway and the version of the instance. 3.0.0-rc.2 (2026-11-18) Prerelease: it doesn't move latest . Uses @lambdaorm/lib 3.5.2. Bug Fixes (from @lambdaorm/lib 3.5.1 / 3.5.2): like(p.name, 'Ch%') with the pattern written in the query, p.name.includes('ch') ("contains"), and startsWith / includes with the value in a variable work on every SQL engine. The date functions ( year , month , day , addDay , dayDiff , …) on a column work on PostgreSQL. The MCP guide ( lambdaorm://guide/expressions ) and the description of orm_execute teach them; the evaluation set has two more questions (contains, like with _ ). 3.0.0-rc.1 (2026-11-18) First release of the Data Gateway, published as the Docker image flaviorita/data-gateway . Prerelease: it doesn't move latest . Uses @lambdaorm/lib 3.5.0. Features: One mandatory configuration file ( DATA_GATEWAY_CONFIG_PATH , default /config/data-gateway.config.yaml ), with environment variables anywhere in it. Transports by configuration, each on its own port, none by default: http (the REST API), mcpHttp (MCP Streamable HTTP, stateless or stateful, plus the deprecated HTTP+SSE), mcpWebSocket and webSocket (JSON-RPC with notifications). MCP: 22 tools (one per operation, writes included) listed by the credential's permissions, with readOnlyHint / destructiveHint , the domain in the description of orm_execute , resources ( lambdaorm://guide/expressions , the domain, each entity) and mcp.maxRows . Several schemas: discovered under orm.workspacePath (the folder is the route: /iot/v1 ) and declared in orm.schemas , with overrides per schema (transports, authentication, env, scripts, mcp, server, runtime). Each schema worker receives only its own variables. Runtime: a supervisor, an edge worker with the transports and a worker per schema ( thread or process ); heartbeat, restarts with a growing wait, server.maxConcurrent (429) and server.maxResponseBytes (413). A schema that doesn't start or falls doesn't affect the others; at start each schema checks a connection of each source. Credentials with permissions ( read , write , script , queue , stageImport ) for bearer, API key and basic; a write with only read is refused before connecting. Audit of writes, scripts, queued executions and stage imports (a JSON line "type":"audit" on stdout). The query UI at /ui ( transports.http.ui.enabled , off by default), built on @lambdaorm/ui ; GET /typings and GET /whoami per schema. Metrics of every worker in /metrics (and /{schema}/metrics ); logs labeled by worker. The image runs node index.js (it stops on SIGTERM ). Known limits (of @lambdaorm/lib , avoided by the MCP guide): like with a literal pattern, includes over text, grouping by an expression, the sql.js adapter. Fixed in rc.2.

docs.text: Clients Node: @lambdaorm/client @lambdaorm/client has the same interface as the library ( orm.execute , orm.plan , orm.executeScript , …) and runs it on a Data Gateway. The URL includes the schema's route; http(s):// uses the REST API and ws(s):// the WebSocket API . npm install @lambdaorm/client import { orm } from '@lambdaorm/client' // REST, an API key await orm.init('http://gateway:8080/iot/v1', { headers: { 'X-Api-Key': process.env.IOT_KEY } }) const devices = await orm.execute('Devices.filter(p => p.status == status)', { status: 'active' }) // a bearer token: sent as Authorization: Bearer <token> await orm.init('http://gateway:8080/iot/v1', { token: process.env.IOT_TOKEN }) Over WebSocket, every operation uses one persistent connection, and orm.on receives the notifications ( queue.completed , queue.failed , schema.statusChanged ): await orm.init('ws://gateway:8083/iot/v1', { headers: { 'X-Api-Key': process.env.IOT_KEY } }) const stop = orm.on('schema.statusChanged', state => console.log(state.path, state.status, state.reason)) const products = await orm.execute('Products.filter(p => p.price > minPrice)', { minPrice: 50 }) // … stop() await orm.end() // closes the connection With a single schema at the root, the URL is the gateway's: http://gateway:8080 . CLI The CLI runs its commands locally with a workspace ( -w ) or on a Data Gateway with -u and the schema's URL. With bearer authentication, the token is taken from the SERVICE_TOKEN environment variable: export SERVICE_TOKEN=… lambdaorm execute -q "Devices.filter(p => p.status == 'active')" -u http://gateway:8080/iot/v1 lambdaorm script -x "orm.execute(\"Devices.map(p => count(1))\")" -u http://gateway:8080/iot/v1 Other languages The OpenAPI 3 document of the REST API is served by the gateway ( /doc , /api-docs ): a client for any language can be generated from it with OpenAPI Generator . AI agents Through MCP : claude mcp add --transport http iot-v1 http://gateway:8081/iot/v1/mcp --header "X-Api-Key: $KEY" Web The UI of the gateway, and @lambdaorm/ui to put it in an application of your own.

docs.text: Configuration Everything is configured in one YAML file , mounted in the container, never baked into the image: Path: DATA_GATEWAY_CONFIG_PATH (default /config/data-gateway.config.yaml ). It is mandatory : without it the gateway logs the error and exits with code 1. An invalid key or value also stops the start, with the list of problems. $VAR and ${VAR} are replaced by environment variables anywhere in the file, also inside a text ( "${HOST}:${PORT}" ). A variable that is not defined counts as not set : a transport whose port: $VAR is not defined is not exposed; a credential whose secret is not defined stops the start. The λORM schemas ( lambdaORM.yaml , sources, mappings, stages, queue) stay in their workspaces. The gateway's file says where they are, how each one is reached and how it is exposed. Transports and ports A transport is exposed only when it has a port . There are no default ports, neither in the code nor in the image: transports.<name> Result missing not exposed present without port , or port: $VAR with the variable not defined not exposed (logged: mcpHttp not exposed: no port configured ) port that is not an integer 1–65535 configuration error: the gateway doesn't start two transports on the same host:port configuration error no transport exposed at all configuration error So the same file can expose MCP only where DATA_GATEWAY_MCP_PORT is defined. The transports are described in Transports . Schemas A schema is a λORM workspace (a folder with lambdaORM.yaml ) served at a route ( iot/v1 ). They are declared in two ways, which can be combined. Discovered ( orm.workspacePath ). The folder is walked at start: every folder with a lambdaORM.yaml is a schema and its relative path is its route. Below a schema the walk stops (a workspace has folders of its own). /workspace (orm.workspacePath) ├── iot/ │ ├── v1/lambdaORM.yaml → schema "iot/v1" → /iot/v1/... │ └── v2/lambdaORM.yaml → schema "iot/v2" → /iot/v2/... └── accounts/ └── v1/lambdaORM.yaml → schema "accounts/v1" → /accounts/v1/... Declared ( orm.schemas[] with workspace ). The route doesn't depend on where the folder is: one volume per schema, or an instance that serves only some schemas. orm: workspacePath: /workspace schemas: - path: accounts/v1 workspace: /mnt/accounts # a folder with lambdaORM.yaml, or the file itself Adjusted. An entry of orm.schemas[] without workspace adjusts a discovered schema (its path must match one). What a schema can adjust: Key of a schema Effect If not set transports the transports that expose it; on the others its routes don't exist ( 404 ) every exposed transport authentication replaces the authentication (and its permissions) for this schema, on all its transports the transport's, else the global one env variables its worker receives (below) its .env and the base variables scripts enabled and the limits of scripts scripts mcp.maxRows , mcp.tools row limit and tools of its MCP server mcp server.timeout , server.maxConcurrent , server.maxResponseBytes timeout, simultaneous operations and response size server runtime.mode , runtime.maxMemoryMb , runtime.checkConnections thread / process , memory of its worker, whether its connections are checked at start runtime The most specific always wins and replaces the others: schema → transport → global. Rules: At least one of orm.workspacePath or a orm.schemas[] with workspace , and at least one schema. Two schemas with the same route, or a route that is the prefix of another ( iot and iot/v1 ), are an error. Each segment of a route: [a-zA-Z0-9_.-] , and none of the reserved names: health , ping , metrics , version , schemas , mcp , sse , messages , status , doc , api-docs , swagger , asyncapi , ui , whoami , typings . A schema at the root: if workspacePath itself has a lambdaORM.yaml (or a declared schema uses path: "" ), it is served at the root ( /execute ). Only when it is the only schema. No hot reload: a new schema is taken when the gateway restarts. Each schema uses the infrastructure.queue (Kafka) of its own lambdaORM.yaml , if it has one. Environment of each schema λORM replaces the $VAR of a lambdaORM.yaml with the environment. So that a schema cannot read another one's credentials nor the gateway's secrets, each schema worker receives only its own variables , from highest to lowest priority: Source Example schemas[].env in the gateway's file (the values can use the gateway's variables) DB_CONNECTION: $IOT_V1_DB a .env file in the schema's workspace (optional) /workspace/iot/v1/.env the base variables: PATH , HOME , TZ , LANG , NODE_* , LD_LIBRARY_PATH , ORACLE_* , and runtime.env.passthrough TZ=UTC Every lambdaORM.yaml can use the same names, and the gateway maps each one to its real secret: orm: workspacePath: /workspace schemas: - path: iot/v1 env: { DB_CONNECTION: $IOT_V1_DB } - path: iot/v2 env: { DB_CONNECTION: $IOT_V2_DB } # iot/v2 can be an exact copy of iot/v1 runtime: env: isolate: true # false: every schema gets the whole environment (local development) passthrough: [ KAFKA_BROKER ] # variables every schema receives A variable used in schemas[].env that is not defined stays undefined: that schema fails to connect and is shown in error with the reason; the others start. Runtime runtime: schemas: thread # thread | process: one worker per schema (runtime.mode adjusts one schema) maxMemoryMb: 512 # JavaScript heap of each worker; above it, only that worker is restarted checkConnections: true # at start each schema opens a connection of each source: a database down → error, retried threadpoolSize: auto # UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE; auto = max(4, 2 × schemas in thread mode), at most 64 heartbeat: intervalMs: 5000 timeoutMs: 30000 # a worker that doesn't answer is ended and restarted restart: initialDelayMs: 1000 # first wait before retrying a fallen worker or a schema that didn't start maxDelayMs: 300000 # the wait grows up to this env: { isolate: true, passthrough: [] } What each mode isolates: thread process another instance CPU and event loop yes yes yes JavaScript heap ( maxMemoryMb ) yes yes yes A hung worker (heartbeat) yes yes yes Environment variables yes yes yes libuv thread pool (DNS, fs , native drivers) shared ( threadpoolSize ) yes yes Native memory, container OOM no same container yes A crash of native code no: the whole process yes yes thread suits development and small schemas; runtime.mode: process a critical schema in production (Oracle in thick mode uses native code); a separate instance, schemas of different teams or customers. Complete example # data-gateway.config.yaml orm: workspacePath: /workspace schemas: - path: iot/v1 # discovered: only adjustments transports: [ http ] # not exposed by MCP env: { DB_CONNECTION: $IOT_V1_DB } scripts: { enabled: false } - path: iot/v2 env: { DB_CONNECTION: $IOT_V2_DB } mcp: { maxRows: 100 } runtime: { maxMemoryMb: 1024 } - path: accounts/v1 # declared: defines and adjusts workspace: /mnt/accounts env: { DB_CONNECTION: $ACCOUNTS_DB } runtime: { mode: process } authentication: adapter: local type: apikey keys: - { name: accounts-backend, value: $ACCOUNTS_KEY, permissions: [ read, write ] } runtime: schemas: thread maxMemoryMb: 512 server: timeout: 120000 # ms per request, message or tool call maxConcurrent: 64 # simultaneous operations per schema; above it, 429 requestBodySize: 14MB maxResponseBytes: 256MB # 0 = no limit logger: { adapter: console, level: info } metrics: { enabled: true } audit: { enabled: true, includeData: false } authentication: # for every schema and transport that doesn't set its own adapter: local type: apikey header: X-Api-Key keys: - { name: agent, value: $AGENT_KEY, permissions: [ read ] } - { name: backend, value: $BACKEND_KEY, permissions: [ read, write, script, queue, stageImport ] } rateLimit: { windowMs: 30000, max: 0 } # http only; max: 0 = no rate limit scripts: { enabled: true, maxLength: 20000, timeoutMs: 30000, maxIterations: 100000 } mcp: name: data-gateway tools: { include: [], exclude: [] } pageSize: 50 maxRows: 500 transports: http: port: $DATA_GATEWAY_HTTP_PORT ui: { enabled: true } mcpHttp: port: $DATA_GATEWAY_MCP_HTTP_PORT mcpWebSocket: port: $DATA_GATEWAY_MCP_WS_PORT webSocket: port: $DATA_GATEWAY_WS_PORT Reference Key Default Notes orm.workspacePath — the folder where schemas are discovered orm.schemas[] [] path (mandatory), workspace (defines a schema) and adjustments runtime.schemas thread thread / process runtime.maxMemoryMb 512 per worker runtime.checkConnections true a database down leaves the schema in error , retried, instead of failing in the first query runtime.threadpoolSize auto max(4, 2 × schemas in thread mode) , at most 64 runtime.heartbeat.intervalMs / timeoutMs 5000 / 30000 runtime.restart.initialDelayMs / maxDelayMs 1000 / 300000 growing wait between restarts runtime.env.isolate / passthrough true / [] server.timeout 120000 per HTTP request, WebSocket message and MCP tool call server.maxConcurrent 64 simultaneous operations per schema; above it 429 ; 0 = no limit server.requestBodySize 14MB server.maxResponseBytes 256MB above it, 413 ; 0 = no limit logger.adapter / logger.level console / info console or winston ; error , warn , info , debug metrics.enabled true audit.enabled true the audit of writes ( Security ) audit.includeData false true adds the parameters ( data ), which can have personal data authentication { adapter: none } Security transports.<t>.authentication authentication replaces the global one for that transport rateLimit.windowMs / rateLimit.max 30000 / 30 http only; max: 0 turns it off scripts.enabled false POST /script and its tool and method scripts.maxLength / timeoutMs / maxIterations 20000 / 30000 / 100000 a request can ask for less, never more mcp.name data-gateway the name of the MCP servers; each one adds its route mcp.tools.include / exclude [] / [] names of tools mcp.pageSize 50 page of tools/list and resources/list mcp.maxRows 500 rows of orm_execute / orm_execute_script ; 0 = no limit transports.<t>.port none without a port, the transport is not exposed transports.<t>.host 0.0.0.0 transports.<t>.basePath '' a prefix before the schema's route ( /data-gateway ), behind an ingress with a path transports.<t>.maxConnections 100 webSocket , mcpWebSocket and the SSE of mcpHttp transports.http.swagger.enabled true /doc and /api-docs transports.http.ui.enabled false the UI at /ui transports.mcpHttp.legacySse true besides Streamable HTTP, the older HTTP+SSE for older clients transports.mcpHttp.stateful false stateless Streamable HTTP: any replica answers any request transports.<ws>.asyncapi.enabled true GET /asyncapi and /asyncapi.json of webSocket and mcpWebSocket

docs.text: # data-gateway.config.yaml orm: workspacePath: /workspace schemas: - path: iot/v1 # discovered: only adjustments transports: [ http ] # not exposed by MCP env: { DB_CONNECTION: $IOT_V1_DB } scripts: { enabled: false } - path: iot/v2 env: { DB_CONNECTION: $IOT_V2_DB } mcp: { maxRows: 100 } runtime: { maxMemoryMb: 1024 } - path: accounts/v1 # declared: defines and adjusts workspace: /mnt/accounts env: { DB_CONNECTION: $ACCOUNTS_DB } runtime: { mode: process } authentication: adapter: local type: apikey keys: - { name: accounts-backend, value: $ACCOUNTS_KEY, permissions: [ read, write ] } runtime: schemas: thread maxMemoryMb: 512 server: timeout: 120000 # ms per request, message or tool call maxConcurrent: 64 # simultaneous operations per schema; above it, 429 requestBodySize: 14MB maxResponseBytes: 256MB # 0 = no limit logger: { adapter: console, level: info } metrics: { enabled: true } audit: { enabled: true, includeData: false } authentication: # for every schema and transport that doesn't set its own adapter: local type: apikey header: X-Api-Key keys: - { name: agent, value: $AGENT_KEY, permissions: [ read ] } - { name: backend, value: $BACKEND_KEY, permissions: [ read, write, script, queue, stageImport ] } rateLimit: { windowMs: 30000, max: 0 } # http only; max: 0 = no rate limit scripts: { enabled: true, maxLength: 20000, timeoutMs: 30000, maxIterations: 100000 } mcp: name: data-gateway tools: { include: [], exclude: [] } pageSize: 50 maxRows: 500 transports: http: port: $DATA_GATEWAY_HTTP_PORT ui: { enabled: true } mcpHttp: port: $DATA_GATEWAY_MCP_HTTP_PORT mcpWebSocket: port: $DATA_GATEWAY_MCP_WS_PORT webSocket: port: $DATA_GATEWAY_WS_PORT

docs.text: Getting started This guide goes from an empty folder to the northwind database published by a Data Gateway: its REST API, its web UI, MCP for an AI agent and its WebSocket API. It takes about ten minutes and needs only Docker (with Docker Compose). 1. The files Create a folder with this layout (the files can be downloaded from this wiki): northwind/ ├── docker-compose.yml ← PostgreSQL and the Data Gateway ├── data-gateway.config.yaml ← how the gateway exposes the schema and who can use it ├── data.json ← the rows of northwind, to import └── workspace/ └── lambdaORM.yaml ← the λORM schema: domain, mapping, source, stage mkdir -p northwind/workspace && cd northwind W=https://lambda-orm.github.io/wiki/data-gateway/northwind curl -sO $W/docker-compose.yml curl -sO $W/data-gateway.config.yaml curl -sO $W/data.json curl -s $W/lambdaORM.yaml -o workspace/lambdaORM.yaml The schema: workspace/lambdaORM.yaml A normal λORM schema : the domain (entities, properties, relations), the mapping to the tables, one source (PostgreSQL) and the stage default . An excerpt: domain: entities: - name: Products primaryKey: ["id"] uniqueKey: ["name", "supplierId"] properties: - { name: id, type: integer, required: true, autoIncrement: true } - { name: name, required: true } - { name: categoryId, type: integer } - { name: price, type: decimal, default: 0 } relations: - { name: category, from: categoryId, entity: Categories, to: id, target: products } # … Categories, Customers, Orders, Orders.details infrastructure: mappings: - name: default entities: - name: Products mapping: Products properties: - { name: id, mapping: ProductID } - { name: name, mapping: ProductName } # … sources: - name: Northwind dialect: PostgreSQL mapping: default connection: ${NORTHWIND_DB} # an environment variable: the gateway gives it to this schema stages: - name: default sources: - name: Northwind The gateway: data-gateway.config.yaml orm: workspacePath: /workspace # the folder with lambdaORM.yaml (a single schema: served at the root) schemas: - path: "" # that schema: it receives only the variables given here env: { NORTHWIND_DB: $NORTHWIND_DB } authentication: adapter: local type: apikey header: X-Api-Key keys: - { name: reader, value: $READER_KEY, permissions: [ read ] } - { name: backend, value: $BACKEND_KEY, permissions: [ read, write, script, queue, stageImport ] } scripts: enabled: true transports: http: port: 8080 ui: { enabled: true } mcpHttp: port: 8081 webSocket: port: 8083 Two credentials: reader can only read; backend can also write, run scripts, queue and import. Three transports: REST and the UI on 8080, MCP on 8081, WebSocket on 8083. The variables of the schema: each schema receives only its own variables, for its safety; env gives it the connection. docker-compose.yml services: postgres: image: postgres:16-alpine environment: POSTGRES_USER: northwind POSTGRES_PASSWORD: northwind POSTGRES_DB: northwind healthcheck: test: [ "CMD", "pg_isready", "-U", "northwind" ] interval: 2s retries: 30 data-gateway: image: flaviorita/data-gateway:3.0.0-rc.4 depends_on: postgres: { condition: service_healthy } environment: NORTHWIND_DB: '{"host":"postgres","port":5432,"user":"northwind","password":"northwind","database":"northwind"}' READER_KEY: ${READER_KEY:-reader-demo-key} BACKEND_KEY: ${BACKEND_KEY:-backend-demo-key} volumes: - ./data-gateway.config.yaml:/config/data-gateway.config.yaml:ro - ./workspace:/workspace ports: - "${HTTP_PORT:-8080}:8080" - "${MCP_PORT:-8081}:8081" - "${WS_PORT:-8083}:8083" The keys reader-demo-key and backend-demo-key are for this example only: in any real use, give READER_KEY and BACKEND_KEY long random values ( openssl rand -hex 24 ). 2. Start it docker compose up -d curl http://localhost:8080/schemas [ { "path": "", "status": "ready", "since": "2026-11-18T14:07:33.561Z", "restarts": 0 } ] The schema is ready : it is served at the root ( /execute , /mcp , …). If it says error , reason tells why (a database that can't be reached, a variable not given); the gateway keeps retrying. 3. Create the tables The image includes the λORM CLI . push creates the tables of the stage from the schema: docker compose exec data-gateway lambdaorm push -w /workspace -s default create table Categories … add foreign key Order Details_product_FK 4. Import the data, through the REST API The import needs the stageImport permission, so reader can't: curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/stages/default/import -H "X-Api-Key: reader-demo-key" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @data.json { "error": "ForbiddenError", "message": "the credential \"reader\" does not have the \"stageImport\" permission" } and backend can (it answers 204 , and the import leaves an audit line in the log): curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/stages/default/import -H "X-Api-Key: backend-demo-key" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @data.json docker compose logs data-gateway | grep '"type":"audit"' {"type":"audit","time":"2026-11-18T14:07:39.720Z","schema":"","transport":"http","credential":"backend","operation":"stageImport","stage":"default","durationMs":189,"result":"ok"} 5. Query curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/execute?format=beautiful" -H "X-Api-Key: reader-demo-key" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "query": "Products.filter(p => p.price > minPrice).map(p => ({ name: p.name, category: p.category.name, price: p.price })).sort(p => desc(p.price)).page(1, 3)", "data": { "minPrice": 50 } }' [ { "name": "Côte de Blaye", "category": "Beverages", "price": 263.5 }, { "name": "Thüringer Rostbratwurst", "category": "Meat/Poultry", "price": 123.79 }, { "name": "Mishi Kobe Niku", "category": "Meat/Poultry", "price": 97 } ] p.category.name follows the relation: λORM joins Categories . plan shows how, without running it: curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/plan?format=beautiful" -H "X-Api-Key: reader-demo-key" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"query": "Products.filter(p => p.price > minPrice).map(p => ({ name: p.name, category: p.category.name, price: p.price })).sort(p => desc(p.price)).page(1, 3)"}' { "entity": "Products", "dialect": "PostgreSQL", "source": "Northwind", "sentence": "SELECT p.ProductName AS \"name\", c.CategoryName AS \"category\", p.UnitPrice AS \"price\" FROM Products p INNER JOIN Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID WHERE p.UnitPrice > $1 ORDER BY p.UnitPrice desc OFFSET 0 LIMIT 3 " } 6. Write, and the permissions A query that writes, with reader : curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/execute -H "X-Api-Key: reader-demo-key" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"query": "Products.update(p => ({ price: price })).filter(p => p.id == id)", "data": {"id": 38, "price": 270}}' { "error": "ForbiddenError", "message": "the credential \"reader\" does not have the \"write\" permission" } The gateway refused it before reaching the database , because the query is not a select. With backend it answers the rows updated, 1 , and leaves an audit line. 7. A script: several queries in one transaction curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/script?format=beautiful" -H "X-Api-Key: backend-demo-key" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "script": "orders = orm.execute(\"Orders.filter(p => p.customerId == customerId).map(p => p.id)\", { customerId: customerId }); { customer: customerId, orders: orders.length() }", "data": { "customerId": "ALFKI" } }' { "customer": "ALFKI", "orders": 6 } A script chooses the status of the answer with throw { status, message } : a customer not found with status: 404 answers 404 . See Script . 8. The API documentation http://localhost:8080/doc/ is the Swagger UI of the REST API. Authorize asks for the API key in the X-Api-Key header; then every method can be tried from the page. 9. The UI Open http://localhost:8080/ui/ : Login with the API key (the Show button shows what was typed): On the left, the explorer : the schema, its domain, its entities with their properties and relations. Choose the schema / , write a query (the editor completes the entities and properties as you type), its data, and execute (Ctrl+Enter). The result can be seen as a table, tree, JSON or YAML, copied and exported: Save it with Ctrl+S: a name, a description and a folder (folders are created with the + of the schema): A double click on an entity (or its Open button) shows its form : properties, relations, keys and indexes, its rows and its diagram. A diagram: the + of a folder → New diagram , choose Orders and Add their neighbours : The boxes are laid out by themselves; they and the lines can be dragged, and Save keeps them where they were left: Everything is explained in UI . 10. An AI agent, through MCP With Claude Code : claude mcp add --transport http northwind http://localhost:8081/mcp --header "X-Api-Key: reader-demo-key" Then ask it, for example, "how many products does each category have?" . The agent sees the tools the reader credential can use ( orm_execute , orm_plan , schema_domain , …; not the ones that write), with the domain of northwind in their descriptions, and answers with a query like: { "name": "orm_execute", "arguments": { "query": "Categories.map(p => ({ category: p.name, products: count(p.products.id) }))" } } [ { "category": "Grains/Cereals", "products": 7 }, { "category": "Beverages", "products": 12 }, … ] With reader , the agent cannot change anything, whatever it is asked. See MCP . 11. WebSocket One connection for every operation, with notifications. With @lambdaorm/client : import { orm } from '@lambdaorm/client' await orm.init('ws://localhost:8083/', { headers: { 'X-Api-Key': 'reader-demo-key' } }) const customers = await orm.execute('Customers.filter(p => p.country == country).map(p => p.name)', { country: 'Argentina' }) // [ { name: 'Cactus Comidas para llevar' }, { name: 'Océano Atlántico Ltda.' }, { name: 'Rancho grande' } ] await orm.end() or the JSON-RPC messages themselves: → { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "query.execute", "params": { "query": "Customers.filter(p => p.country == country).map(p => p.name)", "data": { "country": "Argentina" } } } ← { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": [ { "name": "Cactus Comidas para llevar" }, { "name": "Océano Atlántico Ltda." }, { "name": "Rancho grande" } ] } See WebSocket API . 12. Stop it docker compose down # keeps nothing: the database is in the container Next steps Several schemas, one route each, and the environment of each: Configuration . Credentials per schema or per transport, the audit, the limits: Security . Every REST method: REST API . Production: Operations .

docs.text: MCP The gateway is a Model Context Protocol server, so AI agents (Claude Code and any MCP client) can explore the domain and query the data with λORM's language. There is one MCP server per schema ( /iot/v1/mcp ): its tools describe that schema's domain, and each version is registered as a separate server in the client ( iot-v1 , iot-v2 ). claude mcp add --transport http iot-v1 http://localhost:8081/iot/v1/mcp --header "X-Api-Key: $KEY" With a single schema at the root: http://localhost:8081/mcp . Tools One tool per operation of the schema, writes included : an agent can do what an application does, if its credential allows it . The descriptions and input schemas are generated when the schema starts and carry its domain (entities, properties, relations, enums), so the model knows what to query without a previous call. Tool Arguments REST equivalent Permission Hint orm_execute query , data? , options? POST /execute read (selects) or write read only with read ; destructive with write orm_execute_script script , data? , options? POST /script script destructive orm_execute_queued topic , query , data? , chunk? , options? POST /execute-queued queue destructive orm_plan query , options? POST /plan read read only orm_metadata query POST /metadata read read only orm_model query POST /model read read only orm_parameters query POST /parameters read read only orm_constraints query POST /constraints read read only schema_get — GET /schema read read only schema_version — GET /schema/version read read only schema_domain — GET /domain read read only schema_entities entity? GET /entities[/{entity}] read read only schema_enums enum? GET /enums[/{enum}] read read only schema_sources source? GET /sources[/{source}] read read only schema_mappings mapping? , entity? GET /mappings… read read only schema_views — GET /views read read only schema_stages stage? GET /stages[/{stage}] read read only stage_exists stage GET /stages/{stage}/exists read read only stage_export stage GET /stages/{stage}/export read read only stage_import stage , data POST /stages/{stage}/import stageImport destructive gateway_version — GET /version read read only gateway_health — GET /health read read only tools/list shows a credential only the tools it can use. Without script , orm_execute_script doesn't appear; with only read , orm_execute is described as "read-only queries with this credential". The hints ( readOnlyHint , destructiveHint ) don't block anything: they tell the client which tools change data, so it can ask for confirmation. What blocks is the permissions . The same rules as REST: orm_execute_script fails if scripts are disabled; orm_execute_queued , if the schema has no queue. mcp.tools.include / exclude (global or per schema) restrict the list further, for example exclude: [ orm_execute_script, stage_import ] . Results and errors A result is { content: [{ type: "text", text: <JSON> }] } , with structuredContent too when it is small. Row limit ( mcp.maxRows , default 500). When orm_execute or orm_execute_script answer a longer list, it is cut and the model is told how to ask for less: json { "rows": [ "…500 rows…" ], "truncated": true, "returned": 500, "total": 18234, "hint": "The result was cut to 500 rows. Use .page(1, 500) (or a smaller page), aggregate with map/count, or filter the query more." } It applies only to MCP and after the query ran: it protects the model's context. The database is protected by server.maxResponseBytes and server.timeout . - An error of λORM (syntax, an unknown entity, a constraint, a disabled script) or a missing permission answers isError: true with the message, so the model can read it and correct the query. Resources URI Content lambdaorm://guide/expressions a short guide of the query language (Markdown), to give the model context lambdaorm://schema/domain the whole domain of the schema, JSON lambdaorm://entities/{entity} one entity (template) What an agent can do There is no read-only mode of the transport: what an agent can do is decided by its credential's permissions . An agent that only queries gets a credential with [ read ] : it can run selects but not write, run scripts, queue or import, by any transport. Besides: schemas[].transports to keep a schema out of MCP, mcp.tools.exclude , the hints, and the permissions of the database user (the guarantee underneath). Every write an agent makes is audited with the name of its credential and "transport": "mcpHttp" . Transports mcpHttp Route Protocol POST/GET/DELETE {basePath}/{schema}/mcp Streamable HTTP: Claude Code --transport http and current clients GET {basePath}/{schema}/sse + POST {basePath}/{schema}/messages?sessionId=<id> HTTP+SSE (deprecated), with legacySse: true GET {basePath}/status the state of the transport, the schemas and the open SSE sessions Streamable HTTP is stateless by default ( stateful: false ): each POST stands alone and any replica answers it. The credential goes in every request. mcpWebSocket An upgrade at {basePath}/{schema}/mcp , authenticated in the handshake; JSON-RPC 2.0 messages with the MCP methods ( initialize , ping , tools/list , tools/call , resources/list , resources/read , …). It is not a standard MCP transport: it is offered for clients and gateways that support it on their own. Its AsyncAPI document is at GET {basePath}/asyncapi . → { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/call", "params": { "name": "orm_execute", "arguments": { "query": "Products.filter(p => p.price > 50).map(p => p.name)" } } } ← { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": { "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": "[\"Côte de Blaye\", \"Thüringer Rostbratwurst\"]" } ] } }
docs.title: MCP

docs.text: The gateway is a Model Context Protocol server, so AI agents (Claude Code and any MCP client) can explore the domain and query the data with λORM's language. There is one MCP server per schema ( /iot/v1/mcp ): its tools describe that schema's domain, and each version is registered as a separate server in the client ( iot-v1 , iot-v2 ). claude mcp add --transport http iot-v1 http://localhost:8081/iot/v1/mcp --header "X-Api-Key: $KEY" With a single schema at the root: http://localhost:8081/mcp .
docs.title: MCP

docs.text: One tool per operation of the schema, writes included : an agent can do what an application does, if its credential allows it . The descriptions and input schemas are generated when the schema starts and carry its domain (entities, properties, relations, enums), so the model knows what to query without a previous call. Tool Arguments REST equivalent Permission Hint orm_execute query , data? , options? POST /execute read (selects) or write read only with read ; destructive with write orm_execute_script script , data? , options? POST /script script destructive orm_execute_queued topic , query , data? , chunk? , options? POST /execute-queued queue destructive orm_plan query , options? POST /plan read read only orm_metadata query POST /metadata read read only orm_model query POST /model read read only orm_parameters query POST /parameters read read only orm_constraints query POST /constraints read read only schema_get — GET /schema read read only schema_version — GET /schema/version read read only schema_domain — GET /domain read read only schema_entities entity? GET /entities[/{entity}] read read only schema_enums enum? GET /enums[/{enum}] read read only schema_sources source? GET /sources[/{source}] read read only schema_mappings mapping? , entity? GET /mappings… read read only schema_views — GET /views read read only schema_stages stage? GET /stages[/{stage}] read read only stage_exists stage GET /stages/{stage}/exists read read only stage_export stage GET /stages/{stage}/export read read only stage_import stage , data POST /stages/{stage}/import stageImport destructive gateway_version — GET /version read read only gateway_health — GET /health read read only tools/list shows a credential only the tools it can use. Without script , orm_execute_script doesn't appear; with only read , orm_execute is described as "read-only queries with this credential". The hints ( readOnlyHint , destructiveHint ) don't block anything: they tell the client which tools change data, so it can ask for confirmation. What blocks is the permissions . The same rules as REST: orm_execute_script fails if scripts are disabled; orm_execute_queued , if the schema has no queue. mcp.tools.include / exclude (global or per schema) restrict the list further, for example exclude: [ orm_execute_script, stage_import ] .
docs.title: Tools

docs.text: A result is { content: [{ type: "text", text: <JSON> }] } , with structuredContent too when it is small. Row limit ( mcp.maxRows , default 500). When orm_execute or orm_execute_script answer a longer list, it is cut and the model is told how to ask for less: json { "rows": [ "…500 rows…" ], "truncated": true, "returned": 500, "total": 18234, "hint": "The result was cut to 500 rows. Use .page(1, 500) (or a smaller page), aggregate with map/count, or filter the query more." } It applies only to MCP and after the query ran: it protects the model's context. The database is protected by server.maxResponseBytes and server.timeout . - An error of λORM (syntax, an unknown entity, a constraint, a disabled script) or a missing permission answers isError: true with the message, so the model can read it and correct the query.
docs.title: Results and errors

docs.text: URI Content lambdaorm://guide/expressions a short guide of the query language (Markdown), to give the model context lambdaorm://schema/domain the whole domain of the schema, JSON lambdaorm://entities/{entity} one entity (template)

docs.text: There is no read-only mode of the transport: what an agent can do is decided by its credential's permissions . An agent that only queries gets a credential with [ read ] : it can run selects but not write, run scripts, queue or import, by any transport. Besides: schemas[].transports to keep a schema out of MCP, mcp.tools.exclude , the hints, and the permissions of the database user (the guarantee underneath). Every write an agent makes is audited with the name of its credential and "transport": "mcpHttp" .

docs.text: Operations Docker The image is flaviorita/data-gateway : Node 24, the lambdaorm CLI and the Oracle Instant Client. It runs node index.js as the user 1000, reads the configuration from /config/data-gateway.config.yaml ( DATA_GATEWAY_CONFIG_PATH ) and the workspaces from where the configuration says ( /workspace by convention). It has no EXPOSE : the ports are only in the configuration. # docker-compose.yml services: data-gateway: image: flaviorita/data-gateway:3.0.0-rc.4 environment: DATA_GATEWAY_HTTP_PORT: "8080" DATA_GATEWAY_MCP_PORT: "8081" READER_KEY: ${READER_KEY} BACKEND_KEY: ${BACKEND_KEY} NORTHWIND_DB: ${NORTHWIND_DB} volumes: - ./data-gateway.config.yaml:/config/data-gateway.config.yaml:ro - ./workspace:/workspace:ro ports: [ "8080:8080", "8081:8081" ] healthcheck: test: [ "CMD", "node", "-e", "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:8080/health').then(r => process.exit(r.ok ? 0 : 1), () => process.exit(1))" ] interval: 10s retries: 6 The versions 3.0.0-rc.* are prereleases: they don't move latest . Kubernetes Probes: livenessProbe on GET /ping (the gateway is up), readinessProbe on GET /health ( 200 while some schema is ready ). A probe per schema: GET /{schema}/health . Configuration in a ConfigMap mounted at /config , secrets as environment variables from a Secret ( value: $READER_KEY in the file). Replicas: REST, WebSocket and stateless MCP ( stateful: false ) need no session affinity; the older HTTP+SSE of MCP does. Behind an ingress with a path: transports.<t>.basePath: /data-gateway . Shutdown: SIGTERM stops accepting connections, waits for the operations in progress (up to server.timeout ), closes the queues and the pools, and exits. Give terminationGracePeriodSeconds at least that time. Health Route Answers GET /ping { "message": "pong", "time" } : the gateway answers GET /health 200 while some schema is ready , 503 if none GET /schemas each schema with status ( starting , ready , error , restarting ), reason , since and restarts GET /{schema}/health 200 when that schema is ready , 503 if not GET /status in mcpHttp and mcpWebSocket : the state of the transport A schema in error is retried with a growing wait ( runtime.restart ) and goes back to ready when its database does, without restarting anything else. Metrics GET /metrics answers the metrics of every worker in Prometheus format ( GET /{schema}/metrics , those of one schema), each with the label worker ( edge , schema:iot/v1 ): Metric Labels data_gateway_requests_total transport , schema , method , status , credential data_gateway_request_duration_seconds transport , schema , method data_gateway_forbidden_total credential , permission data_gateway_throttled_total schema , transport (answers 429 by maxConcurrent ) data_gateway_connections transport data_gateway_schema_status schema , status data_gateway_schema_restarts schema data_gateway_event_loop_lag_seconds worker and the usual metrics of Node (memory, CPU, event loop). metrics.enabled: false turns them off. Logs Each worker logs with its label ( [supervisor] , [edge] , [schema:iot/v1] ): the start, the transports exposed or not, the effective configuration without secrets, the states of the schemas, falls and restarts, heartbeats missed, and every operation with the name of its credential (never its secret). logger.level : error , warn , info , debug ; logger.adapter : console or winston . The audit of writes goes to the standard output as JSON lines with "type": "audit" , to be kept apart by the log collector.

docs.text: REST API The http transport ( Transports ) exposes every operation of λORM on a schema as REST, with JSON in and out. The OpenAPI 3 document is served by the gateway at /doc (Swagger UI) and /api-docs . Routes The examples use a gateway at http://localhost:8080 with an API key. Each schema's methods are under its route: Gateway Schema iot/v1 Only schema at the root http://localhost:8080 http://localhost:8080/iot/v1/execute http://localhost:8080/execute With transports.http.basePath: /data-gateway , every route is under it: /data-gateway/iot/v1/execute . Every request needs the credential, except /ping , /health and /metrics (at the root and under each schema), /schemas , /version , /doc and the UI. How it is sent depends on the authentication : X-Api-Key: <key> , Authorization: Bearer <token> or Authorization: Basic <base64> . ?format=beautiful indents the JSON of the answer. data (the parameters of a query) and options (for example { "stage": "default" } ) are JSON objects; JSON text ( "data": "{\"id\": 10}" ) is also accepted. An error answers a status and { "error", "code"?, "message" } ( Errors ). Gateway methods Method Route Answers Credential GET /ping { "message": "pong", "time" } no GET /health 200 while some schema is ready , 503 if none no GET /metrics the metrics of every worker, Prometheus text no GET /version the version of the gateway no GET /schemas each schema with its state no GET /whoami the name and permissions of the credential yes curl http://localhost:8080/schemas [ { "path": "iot/v1", "status": "ready", "since": "2026-11-18T13:35:56.407Z", "restarts": 0 }, { "path": "iot/v2", "status": "error", "reason": "connect ECONNREFUSED 10.0.0.5:5432", "since": "…", "restarts": 3 } ] The states are starting , ready , error and restarting . State of a schema Under each schema's route ( /iot/v1/… ), these answer only about that schema: Method Route Answers GET /{schema}/ping 200 if the schema is ready , 503 if not GET /{schema}/health the state of the schema; 503 if it is not ready GET /{schema}/metrics the metrics of that schema GET /{schema}/version the versions of the gateway and the schema GET /{schema}/whoami the name and permissions of the credential with the authentication of that schema, and whether it has scripts enabled curl http://localhost:8080/iot/v1/whoami -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" { "name": "reader", "permissions": ["read"], "schema": "iot/v1", "scripts": true } The secret of the credential is never answered. Query methods execute POST /{schema}/execute runs a query. The body is { query, data?, options? } . curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/execute?format=beautiful" -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"query": "Orders.filter(p => p.customerId == customerId).include(p => p.details)", "data": {"customerId": "CENTC"}}' [ { "id": 12, "customerId": "CENTC", "orderDate": "1996-07-18T00:00:00.000Z", "details": [ { "orderId": 12, "productId": 21, "unitPrice": 8, "quantity": 10 }, { "orderId": 12, "productId": 37, "unitPrice": 20.8, "quantity": 1 } ] } ] A select answers the rows; update and delete answer the number of affected rows ( 0 when nothing matched); insert answers the inserted data. With only the read permission, a query that writes ( insert , update , delete , upsert , merge , bulk* ) is refused with 403 before reaching the database. curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/execute -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"query": "Orders.update(p => ({ freight: freight })).filter(p => p.id == id)", "data": {"id": 10248, "freight": 40}}' 1 plan POST /{schema}/plan answers how the query is executed: the dialect, the source and the sentence of each part, without running it. Body { query, options? } . curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/plan -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"query": "Orders.filter(p => p.customerId == customerId).include(p => p.details)"}' { "entity": "Orders", "dialect": "PostgreSQL", "source": "default", "sentence": "SELECT o.OrderID AS \"id\", o.CustomerID AS \"customerId\", o.OrderDate AS \"orderDate\", o.OrderID AS \"__id\" FROM Orders o WHERE o.CustomerID = $1 ", "children": [ { "entity": "Orders.details", "dialect": "PostgreSQL", "source": "default", "sentence": "SELECT o1.OrderID AS \"orderId\", o1.ProductID AS \"productId\", o1.UnitPrice AS \"unitPrice\", o1.Quantity AS \"quantity\", o1.OrderID AS \"LambdaOrmParentId\" FROM \"Order Details\" o1 WHERE o1.OrderID IN ($1) " } ] } model POST /{schema}/model answers the shape of the result: its properties and their types. [ { "name": "id", "type": "integer" }, { "name": "customerId", "type": "string" }, { "name": "orderDate", "type": "dateTime" }, { "name": "details", "type": "Orders.details[]", "children": [ { "name": "orderId", "type": "integer" }, { "name": "productId", "type": "integer" }, { "name": "unitPrice", "type": "decimal" }, { "name": "quantity", "type": "decimal" } ] } ] parameters POST /{schema}/parameters answers the variables the query uses, which go in data . [ { "name": "customerId", "type": "string" } ] constraints POST /{schema}/constraints answers the constraints that apply to the entities of the query. { "entity": "Orders", "constraints": [], "children": [ { "entity": "Orders.details", "constraints": [] } ] } metadata POST /{schema}/metadata answers the analysed tree of the query: each sentence with its action ( select , insert , …), entity, columns, parameters and constraints. { "classtype": "Sentence", "name": "select", "entity": "Orders", "columns": [ { "name": "id" } ], "parameters": [ { "name": "customerId", "type": "any" } ], "constraints": [] } script POST /{schema}/script runs a script : several queries and logic in one transaction. Body { script, data?, options? } . It needs scripts.enabled (otherwise 403 ) and the script permission; the limits of scripts apply ( maxLength , timeoutMs , maxIterations ). curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/script -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "script": "order = orm.execute(\"Orders.filter(p => p.id == id)\", { id: id }); if (order.length() == 0) { throw { status: 404, message: \"order not found\" }; } order[0]", "data": { "id": 10248 } }' A script can choose the status of the answer with throw { status, message } . execute-queued POST /{schema}/execute-queued runs a query in the background and sends its result to a Kafka topic, in chunks. It answers at once { "queueId": "…" } ; the messages carry the keys <queueId>-<chunk> . Body { topic, query, data?, chunk?, options? } . It needs the queue permission (and write if the query writes) and an infrastructure.queue in the schema's lambdaORM.yaml . curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/execute-queued -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"query": "Countries.map(p => [p.iso3, p.name])", "topic": "countries", "chunk": 1000}' The queue of a schema is configured in its lambdaORM.yaml ( config is the kafkajs configuration), where consumers can also be declared: infrastructure: queue: config: $QUEUE_CONFIG consumers: - name: syncInsights config: { groupId: group1 } subscribe: { topic: insights-sync, fromBeginning: true } execute: orm.execute(message.query, message.data, { stage: "insights" }) Over the WebSocket API , query.executeQueued with notify: true also tells the connection when the execution ends. Schema methods The model of the schema. They need read . The connections of the sources are never answered. Method Route Answers GET /{schema}/schema the version and the domain of the schema GET /{schema}/schema/version the version of the schema GET /{schema}/domain the domain: entities (properties, relations, keys, indexes, constraints) and enums GET /{schema}/entities the entities GET /{schema}/entities/{entity} one entity GET /{schema}/enums the enums GET /{schema}/enums/{enum} one enum GET /{schema}/sources the sources, with their name and dialect GET /{schema}/sources/{source} one source GET /{schema}/mappings the mappings (entities to tables and columns) GET /{schema}/mappings/{mapping} one mapping GET /{schema}/mappings/{mapping}/{entity} the mapping of one entity GET /{schema}/views the views GET /{schema}/stages the stages, with their sources GET /{schema}/stages/{stage} one stage GET /{schema}/typings the domain as TypeScript declarations ( text/plain ), for an editor's autocompletion curl http://localhost:8080/sources -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" [ { "name": "catalog", "dialect": "PostgreSQL" }, { "name": "accounts", "dialect": "PostgreSQL" } ] curl http://localhost:8080/entities/Categories -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" { "name": "Categories", "primaryKey": ["id"], "uniqueKey": ["name"], "properties": [ { "name": "id", "type": "integer", "required": true, "autoIncrement": true }, { "name": "name", "type": "string", "length": 80, "required": true }, { "name": "description", "type": "string", "length": 1000 } ], "relations": [] } Stage methods Method Route Answers Permission GET /{schema}/stages/{stage}/exists { "exists": true } when the stage was created and its state file exists read GET /{schema}/stages/{stage}/export the rows of every entity of the stage read POST /{schema}/stages/{stage}/import imports rows (the body is an export) into the entities of the stage stageImport curl http://localhost:8080/stages/default/export -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" > data.json curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/stages/default/import -H "X-Api-Key: $BACKEND_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @data.json Summary Operation REST MCP tool WebSocket method Permission execute POST /execute orm_execute query.execute read (selects) / write script POST /script orm_execute_script query.script script execute queued POST /execute-queued orm_execute_queued query.executeQueued queue plan POST /plan orm_plan query.plan read metadata POST /metadata orm_metadata query.metadata read model POST /model orm_model query.model read parameters POST /parameters orm_parameters query.parameters read constraints POST /constraints orm_constraints query.constraints read schema GET /schema schema_get schema.schema read schema version GET /schema/version schema_version schema.version read domain GET /domain schema_domain schema.domain read entities GET /entities[/{entity}] schema_entities schema.entities , schema.entity read enums GET /enums[/{enum}] schema_enums schema.enums , schema.enum read sources GET /sources[/{source}] schema_sources schema.sources , schema.source read mappings GET /mappings[/{mapping}[/{entity}]] schema_mappings schema.mappings , schema.mapping , schema.entityMapping read views GET /views schema_views schema.views read stages GET /stages[/{stage}] schema_stages schema.stages , schema.stage read typings GET /typings — schema.typings read stage exists GET /stages/{stage}/exists stage_exists stage.exists read stage export GET /stages/{stage}/export stage_export stage.export read stage import POST /stages/{stage}/import stage_import stage.import stageImport version GET /version gateway_version general.version — health GET /health gateway_health general.health — ping GET /ping — general.ping —
